transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (BrightPath Product), Ethan Wu (BrightPath Lead Eng), Laura Chen (BrightPath Security), Devon Ortiz (BrightPath ML), Speaker 6

Summary:
Quick POC check-in focused on SDK integration quirks observed by BrightPath, function-calling reliability and structured output schema stability across model rollouts. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide updated examples and fallback/runbook; BrightPath to run schema stability/fuzz tests and schedule latency benchmark on Dedicated pool.

Topics covered:
- SDK usage (websocket vs REST patterns, retry semantics)
- Function/tool-calling edge cases and error semantics
- Structured output / JSON schema drift and validation strategy
- Fallback patterns and graceful degradation during model swaps
- Security question about logs and redaction

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we've got about 45 minutes, quick recap - last week we shipped the function-calling sample and you ran into a couple of edge cases, Maya correct?
[00:18] Maya (BrightPath Product): yeah hi, thanks alex. so we integrated the sample but saw two things: one, the function call sometimes returns a slightly different key name like \"patient_id\" vs \"patientId\" which breaks our parser; two, sometimes the SDK retries and we end up with duplicate webhook events in our pipeline.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): mm hmm okay that first one sounds like schema drift, and the second sounds like retry semantics - may be down to the SDK default backoff or the webhook idempotency headers. we have examples for idempotency but maybe the sample didn't include them.
[00:50] Ethan (BrightPath Eng): yeah we saw duplicate events when the network blips, the SDK would send the request, got ack, but then the post handler also retried. not sure if the client got the ack though, transcription maybe wrong, it's intermittent.
[01:08] Jordan (Redwood SE): quick clar — are you using the JS SDK or our raw REST calls?
[01:12] Ethan: JS SDK via the server-side adapter, node 18.
[01:16] Jordan: okay good — we recently changed the default retry window in 1.5.2, if you pinned to 1.4.x behaviour could differ. Alex: did we note the SDK version in the sample?
[01:26] Alex: i think the sample was 1.5.1, we can push an 1.5.2 snippet that highlights idempotency-key usage.
[01:33] Maya: that would help. on the schema thing, we've got strict validators in our pipeline—any key mismatch causes the whole record to get rejected which is ugly. is there a recommended stable schema contract approach?
[01:45] Priya: yes, two parts: first, we support structured output with model-enforced JSON via function-calling which tends to be more stable than freeform completions. second, for compatibility we recommend versioned envelopes—include a model_schema_version field and always validate against a small tolerance layer that accepts synonyms, e.g., map patientId and patient_id.
[02:05] Laura (BrightPath Security): quick security note — if you recommend idempotency keys we need guidance on what stays in logs. we need to ensure PHI isn't present in logs and how KMS integrates for keying.
[02:18] Priya: totally, Redwood's hosted logs can be redacted — we support PII scrubbing in transit and at rest. for Private deployments you'll have full control over KMS/HSM. we can share the SOC2 + redaction doc.
[02:32] Devon (BrightPath ML): back to the function-calling - we had an example where the model suggested calling a data-enrichment tool but included an unexpected argument name. the SDK serialized it, our schema rejected it. is there a canonical way to declare allowed args?
[02:48] Jordan: yes, the SDK supports registering function schemas and we do strict validation client-side before sending. but if the model returns slightly different keys the function-caller shim can attempt a best-effort mapping by lowercase and underscore normalization. it's not perfect.
[03:02] Ethan: got it, so is the mapping done on client or server side? we'd prefer server-side mapping so we don't leak transformation logic to clients.
[03:09] Priya: we can provide a middleware for your server that normalizes keys and applies a small mapping table. we'll push that as a snippet.
[03:17] Maya: perfect. one more: schema stability across model rollouts — we saw earlier model swap cause extra fields in the JSON, is there a way to pin behaviour?
[03:29] Alex: yes you can pin model version in the request, but we also provide a "compatibility" mode that falls back to a previous schema variant if validation fails. it is part of rollout policy in the console.
[03:41] Laura: does that compatibility fallback store any PII temporarily? our compliance team will want to know retention and access patterns.
[03:48] Priya: fallback doesn't persist inputs longer than your request retention settings. by default hosted retention is 30 days, but enterprise can set shorter; for Private you control retention. we'll include the retention table in the doc we share.
[04:02] Ethan: about retries — can we get a sample showing how the SDK surfaces a transient model error vs a terminal schema rejection? we need to differentiate retries versus immediate client-side alerting.
[04:15] Jordan: existing error types are in the SDK docs under \"Errors and Recovery\". brief run: transient errors include 429/503 with retry-after; schema errors are thrown as ValidationError with a structure payload. we can add a quick code block to the snippet showing the catch block.
[04:31] Speaker 6: (inaudible) ...the webhook headers...
[04:36] Alex: noted, we'll make headers explicit in the sample (idempotency-key, x-rw-attempt).
[04:41] Maya: on function calling reliability, sometimes the model triggers multi-step tool chains — first call the deid tool, then enrichment. if the deid step fails mid-chain we need atomic behavior or compensating actions, is that supported?
[04:56] Priya: good question — we don't have distributed transaction primitives out of the box. recommended pattern: orchestrate externally — use function-calling to return an ordered list of tool intents, run them in your orchestration layer, and if a step fails run compensating calls. we can show a sample orchestration pattern using the SDK.
[05:14] Devon: that's what we've been doing, but it adds latency. can Redwood provide a low-latency orchestration helper or a single-call composite tool?
[05:23] Jordan: we do have a composite tool pattern where you register a composite function that performs multiple steps server-side in your Private deployment, but hosted calls are single-step to avoid long-running ops. for Dedicated we can look at adding a composite wrapper if you need lower latency.
[05:39] Ethan: scheduling a benchmark for that would be great — we need to compare single-call composite in Dedicated vs multi-step orchestration in Hosted.
[05:48] Alex: i'll put that on the action items: schedule a 30-min latency benchmark with dedicated pool.
[05:54] Maya: thanks. smaller item — our validators reject trailing commas; the model sometimes includes them in generated arrays. can we coerce or strip?
[06:05] Priya: yes normalizer middleware will remove trailing commas and do minor cleanup. we'll include a list of tolerant fixes versus outright rejects.
[06:15] Laura: on logs again, we need clarity about what appears in app logs vs audit logs. is there separation?
[06:22] Priya: yes audit logs are separate and immutable; app logs can be configured to redact. we'll share the log schema and retention settings.
[06:32] Ethan: one more technical oddity — when we run larger batch runs the KV cache memory spikes on our side after warmup; is that normal? we saw memory climb, i'm not sure if it's the Redwood client or our own server.
[06:44] Jordan: KV cache usually lives on the runtime side; in Hosted it’s managed. if you see client-side memory growth that could be due to streaming handlers holding references. can you share a flamegraph?
[06:55] Ethan: sure i'll capture and upload.
[07:00] Maya: okay next steps and recap?
[07:03] Alex: recap — Redwood to send updated SDK 1.5.2 snippet with idempotency header examples, normalizer middleware for key mapping + trailing comma removal, and a short runbook for fallback behavior. BrightPath to run schema-fuzz tests (50k requests) and upload results; schedule Dedicated latency benchmark for composite vs orchestrated flows.
[07:21] Alex: any blockers on timelines?
[07:23] Ethan: none, we should be able to run the tests next week.
[07:26] Laura: we'll need the SOC2/redaction docs for legal review before the benchmark — can you get that by Friday?
[07:32] Priya: yes we'll share SOC2 and retention doc by EOD Thursday.
[07:36] Jordan: small note — when you run the fuzz test, include both pinned model and latest variant, that's how we catch drift early.
[07:44] Devon: good idea.
[07:46] Alex: perfect. i'll circulate meeting notes and action items. thanks everyone.
[07:51] Maya: thanks all.
[07:52] (call ends)
